game_files.label: Ultimate Mortal Kombat 3 iOS app (version 1.2.59)
game_files.description: A legally obtained copy of Ultimate Mortal Kombat 3 for iOS, version 1.2.59. Extract the .ipa (which is a ZIP archive) and locate the Mach-O executable at Payload/UMK3.app/UMK3. The binary must be the armv7 slice from the fat binary.
game_files.notes: The .ipa file is a ZIP archive. Extract it and use tools/macho.py to thin the armv7 slice from the fat binary. The tools will guide you through extraction of symbols and source tree reconstruction.

first_run: Verify you have a legally obtained copy of Ultimate Mortal Kombat 3 for iOS version 1.2.59
The game binary must still contain its STABS debug table (cryptid=0, unstripped); verify this with tools/macho.py
Run the extraction pipeline: python tools/macho.py thin <path/to/UMK3> armv7 work/UMK3.armv7
Dump symbols: python tools/macho.py syms work/UMK3.armv7 work/symbols.txt
Dump functions: python tools/macho.py funcs work/UMK3.armv7 work/functions.txt
Rebuild the source tree from STABS: python tools/stabs.py work/UMK3.armv7 work
Note: This is a work-in-progress decompilation. The project is approximately 74.29% complete. No executable game binary will be produced; only verified C source code and tooling for asset analysis.
notes: This is a decompilation and native port in progress, not a finished game. No playable build exists yet.
The project requires your own legally obtained copy of Ultimate Mortal Kombat 3 for iOS version 1.2.59. No game files are distributed.
The binary must be the unstripped armv7 slice with its STABS debug table intact (cryptid=0). This is the only retail build known to have this property.
No game assets (textures, models, audio, game code) are redistributed. All work is reverse engineering and original platform code.

The project uses differential testing against a static ARM-to-C recompiler (tools/armrecomp/recomp.py) as the verification oracle. No function is accepted until it passes this test with zero divergences.

As of the README date, lime/common (109 functions, the portable engine core) is 100% decompiled and verified. gamecode (291 functions) is 100% decompiled. gamecode/logic (the 2,172-function fight engine) is 80.66% decompiled (1,752 functions). The native platform layer (161 functions) is 10% complete.
The original iOS platform layer is not reverse engineered; it is rewritten natively for Windows/Linux.

Two known exceptions: Finch/ (56 functions, OpenAL audio) is a vendored MIT-licensed third-party library; use upstream instead. ROBO1 and ROBO2 are anomalous exports that break several format parsers and require special handling.

game_files.label: Game disc files
game_files.description: Your own copy of Digimon World as a .bin + .cue pair. The .cue file is the small one; the .bin file is the large game data file.
game_files.notes: The port will prompt you to browse for the .cue file on first run. See DISC.md in the repo for exact version requirements and checksums to verify your copy.

first_run: Extract the zip to a location you will keep it, such as C:\Games\Digimon World. Do not run it from inside the zip.
Run Digimon_World_Recompiled.exe. Windows may warn the app is unrecognized; click More info → Run anyway.
Follow the first-run setup. It will offer to download build tools (about 100 MB); leave the box ticked and click Next.
Click Browse Disc and select your .cue file (the small one, not the .bin).
Wait 10–30 minutes while it builds your copy of the game from your disc. This happens only once. It is normal for the launcher to look busy or briefly unresponsive.
Press PLAY. Future launches skip the build and start in seconds.
notes: Controller: plug it in before launching. In the launcher, leave Player 1 on D-Pad. If you switch to Analog, every button stops working—this game only understands the digital controller.
Keyboard: Enter=Start, X=Cross, S=Circle, A=Triangle, Z=Square, arrow keys=D-Pad. Rebind in the launcher's Controls page.
Saving: you can only save by sleeping. Your partner needs the ZZZ bubble over its head, then open the menu and choose Sleep.
Handy keys: F7=save state, F8=rewind, Alt+Enter=fullscreen.
Save states and rewind capture the game as modded. If you take a state with mods on, load it with the same mods on. Use ordinary memory-card saves for the long term.

Widescreen has two known rough edges: for about a second after a wild battle the picture drops back to 4:3 before widening again, and a few interiors were only built as far as the original camera could see, so their edges can be dark (missing scenery on the disc, not a rendering fault).
If the game runs at 4x speed, open the Mods panel and make sure Fast Loading is OFF. It is off by default from 0.1.5 onward.
If you get stuck on the intro movie (runs about two minutes), the Skip all movies cheat is already on by default in cheats.txt and takes you straight to the title.
A save made with Expanded Roster on expects it to stay on. If you turn it off, that save's partner data no longer lines up.

Trigger id collision was fixed in 0.3.4. A save made before this fix may have its recruitment announcements skipped and species raised under the old scheme read as un-raised, but nothing is corrupted.
unsure: Whether the exact USA version/region is required—DISC.md in the repo specifies the required version, but the game_files section does not state a region requirement explicitly.
The exact checksums required for the disc files are stated to be in DISC.md, which this schema does not have access to, so expected_hashes is empty.

mods.notes: Click Mods in the launcher. Sixteen mods are available, all off by default: Expanded Roster (adds 52 raisable Digimon), Trainer (toggles for never hungry/tired/sick/dead, lifespan loss, and training boosts), Perfect Training, Lucky Reels, Training Multiplier (2×–10×), Guaranteed Item Drops, Quality of Life (partner lifespan and world clock speed), Gameplay (tech learning and evolution stat requirements), Widescreen (16:9 or 16:10), Cheats (57 GameShark-style toggles grouped by effect, including infinite HP, freeze clock, max stats, all cards/items), and Fast Loading (off by default and best left off). Turning a mod off restores the original game exactly. A save made with Expanded Roster on expects it to stay on. The Cheats feature can also be controlled via cheats.txt (change [ ] to [x] for any code).

controller_notes: Controller: plug it in before launching. In the launcher, leave the Player 1 toggle on D-Pad. If you switch it to Analog, every button stops working — this game only understands the digital controller, and that is not a bug in the port.
Keyboard: Enter = Start, X = Cross, S = Circle, A = Triangle, Z = Square, arrow keys = D-Pad. Rebind them in the launcher's Controls page.
Handy keys: F7 save state, F8 rewind, Alt+Enter fullscreen.

game_files.label: Ace Combat X disc image (ISO)
game_files.description: Your own dumped copy of Ace Combat X: Skies of Deception (US, ULUS10176) as an ISO file or extracted directory
game_files.notes: The README states the game addresses data by absolute disc sector. You may provide either a raw ISO file or an extracted game/ directory (created via the tools/isoextract.py and tools/cdiextract.py scripts described in the README). The executable will default to game.iso in the current directory if not provided on the command line, or you can set the PSPRECO_ISO environment variable.

game_files.label: Decrypted EBOOT.elf
game_files.description: Your own dumped and decrypted PSP executable from the disc. EBOOT.BIN on the disc is encrypted; you must decrypt it to ELF format using PSP devkit tooling and place it at the repository root.
game_files.notes: This file is required only if you plan to rebuild the recompilation from source. If using the prebuilt release, this file is not needed. The README states: 'Decrypt your own copy to ELF with whatever PSP devkit tooling you already use for that (out of scope here) and place it at the repository root as EBOOT.elf.'

first_run: Extract release.rar to a folder
Extract your disc image (ISO) to a game/ folder using the tools provided, or provide the ISO file directly: python tools/isoextract.py "Ace Combat X.iso" game/
If extracted, optionally unpack the CDI archive for better performance: python tools/cdiextract.py game
Run pspreco-sdl3.exe with the image: pspreco-sdl3.exe generated/image.bin game (or pspreco-sdl3.exe generated/image.bin for game.iso in the current directory)
notes: USA version only (ULUS10176)
The prebuilt release includes generated/image.bin and a compiled pspreco-sdl3.exe; you do not need to recompile
If you wish to rebuild from source, you will need Python 3.10+, clang (or another C11/C++14 compiler), SDL3, and a Vulkan loader
unsure: Whether the prebuilt release's generated/image.bin is included or must be regenerated from EBOOT.elf (the README states it 'deliberately does not ship' it but the release assets do not list separate files)
The exact location where the ISO or extracted game directory should be placed relative to the executable

mods.notes: The Vulkan backend reads PPSSPP-format texture packs. Put the pack's contents (textures.ini and its subdirectories, or a textures.zip) in textures/ULUS10176/ next to the executable, or point PSPRECO_TEXTURES at the directory. Supported formats: png (any colour type and bit depth), dds (DXT1/3/5 and uncompressed 32-bit), and ktx2 (UASTC or ETC1S, with or without Zstandard supercompression). To build a pack, turn on 'Dump textures' under Debug. Every texture the game uploads is written to textures/ULUS10176/new as <hash>.png.

build_steps: Extract the SLUS_208.51 executable from your Ace Combat 5 NTSC-U disc image (ISO or extracted files)

Set Python path: $env:PYTHONPATH = "tools"

Run recompiler: python -m ps2recomp "C:\path\to\SLUS_208.51" -o generated --ida-db config/ida_db.json --ida-seeds config/ida_seeds.json --symbols config/sdk_symbols.json --symbols config/manual_symbols.json --overrides config/overrides.json --hooks config/hooks.json
Build with CMake: cmake -S . -B build/gcc -G Ninja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=C:/msys64/ucrt64/bin/gcc.exe -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=C:/msys64/ucrt64/bin/c++.exe
Build: cmake --build build/gcc

first_run: Extract the G-Diffuser-v1.1.0-windows-x64.zip release to a folder
Launch G-Diffuser.exe

Review the detected ROM, Expansion Kit disk image, and 64DD IPL ROM

The Expansion Kit disk image and 64DD IPL ROM are mandatory — the port includes full Expansion Kit support and Course Edit is not optional
Disk saves are journaled to a separate sidecar file; your original .ndd disk image is never modified
On high-refresh displays (120+ Hz) without vsync capping, enable Frame Pacer in the enhancement menu (F1 > Graphics) to lock the game to 60 FPS

Run the AppImage: ./gen1recomp-0.3.2-linux-x86_64.AppImage

Click 'Choose ROM' (or 'Import ROM' if a file picker appears) and select your legally obtained .gb/.gbc/.gba file

mods.notes: The texture system works through a folder-based workflow: set a texture folder in settings, enable 'Dump textures while playing' to record which textures the game uses, then press 'Process textures' to upscale them using either Lanczos (built-in) or Real-ESRGAN AI (requires a 43 MB download and Vulkan-capable GPU). The upscaled pack loads automatically on the next launch or when F9 is pressed. Per-stage warming records which textures each chapter uses in <texture folder>/pack/stages/ to fit more of a large pack in the texture cache. Toggle the pack live with F9 while playing to compare. Dumping and using the pack are mutually exclusive (they conflict on the GPU thread). See docs/TEXTURE_PACK.md for full details on the dump/upscale/pack pipeline and file format.

game_files.label: Tony Hawk's Project 8 disc image
game_files.description: A disc image (.iso or .img) of your own copy of Tony Hawk's Project 8 for Xbox 360 (2006 retail release). The launcher will read it directly and extract the game data on first run.

first_run: Extract the release archive to a folder where you have write access.
Run the Project8Recomp executable.
The launcher will ask for your disc image. Point it at your .iso or .img file.

The launcher will verify the disc (takes under a second). If it matches the 2006 retail release, it will extract the game data into a game/ folder. This takes a few minutes and can be stopped if needed.
Once extraction completes, the game will start automatically. From then on, running Project8Recomp will go directly to the Play button. Pass --gui to open the launcher settings.
On macOS: the archive is ad-hoc signed but not notarized. Gatekeeper will refuse a double-click. Use Right-click → Open → Open once per install.
notes: Leave the frame rate cap on (default). With it off, in-level cutscenes run 3-5 times too fast.
Heavy scenes on Apple Silicon are functionally correct but slow (4-5 FPS in severe Funpark view). Performance is not comfortable for extended play yet.
The launcher ships with Vulkan runtime and MoltenVK 1.4.2 included; Homebrew is not required.
Only the 2006 retail release (USA/Europe, World v1.0) is supported. Japan v1.0 and other regional variants will be rejected.
Your saves are stored in saves/ and logs in logs/, both inside the extracted folder. Move the entire folder between your own machines and it keeps working.
A previous crash may leave a shared memory segment behind; the launcher will offer a button to free it.

notes: No game data is included in the release archive—you must provide your own legally obtained Rage Racer disc

mods.notes: Extract assets with `rage-extract RAGE.BIN mymod/` to edit PNGs and create a `mod.toml` for texture/material overrides. Point the game at the directory with `--set mods.directory=mymod` or configure `[mods] directory` in rage-port.ini. Edited PNGs are applied as they load. Use `rage-pack mymod/` to pack mods as assets. Material overrides use semantic IDs like `track.big1.terrain.material.3` or `car.0.material.5` with optional `.variant.N` for specificity.

first_run: Extract ogre-battle-64-recomp-linux-x86_64.tar.gz to a folder
Run ./ogrebattle64
On the start screen, click to browse for your ROM file or drag your .z64/.n64/.v64 ROM onto the window

notes: The game requires a 64-bit Linux system with Vulkan 1.2 support
GPU must support Vulkan 1.2 (roughly GeForce GT 630, Radeon HD 7750 (2012) or Intel HD 510 (Skylake) and newer)
CPU must have SSE4.1 support (Intel Core 2 Penryn, AMD Bulldozer or newer)
At least 2 GB RAM required; the emulated N64 machine uses 512 MB
About 150 MB disk space needed for the app, plus the 40 MB ROM
A keyboard is sufficient to play; a gamepad with SDL controller support is optional
Audio device is optional; the game can run silently
If the game crashes on start, update your graphics driver first
Use OGRE_CONSOLE=1 environment variable to see boot logs in a console window on systems without a dedicated console
Use OGRE_GRAPHICS_API environment variable to select graphics backend: 'vulkan', 'd3d12', 'metal', or 'auto' (default)
Battery saves are stored in saves/ folder next to the executable
ROM validation is by hash; the same ROM must be used for saved games to load correctly

build_steps: Clone the repository with submodules: git clone --recursive https://github.com/sciaschi/CBFD-Recompiled.git

Apply patches to tools: git -C tools/N64Recomp apply ../../recomp/n64recomp.patch && git -C tools/N64ModernRuntime apply ../../recomp/n64modernruntime.patch && git -C tools/rt64 apply ../../recomp/rt64.patch
Set up Python virtual environment: python3 -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/pip install -r requirements.txt
Extract ROM assets: cd conker && make extract && make -C conker extract
Build decompilation: make -C conker -j8 && cd ..
Build N64Recomp: cmake -S tools/N64Recomp -B tools/N64Recomp/build -G Ninja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release && cmake --build tools/N64Recomp/build --target N64RecompCLI RSPRecomp RecompModTool
Recompile game functions: sh recomp/run.sh

Build Windows executable: host\build_windows.cmd (Windows) or cmake -S host -B host/build -G Ninja -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=clang -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=clang++ -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=RelWithDebInfo && cmake --build host/build (Linux)

The base port requires only your own disc. HD packs (backgrounds + FMV movies) are optional and auto-detected from hdpacks/ if present beside the executable.
The matching decompilation (byte-exact with the original executables) is enforced on every change. No game executable, BIOS data, or in-game text is distributed in the repo.

mods.notes: Language packs are community-created translations that replace the English text and optionally backgrounds/FMV movies. Packs go in a langpacks/<pack-name>/ folder beside the executable. Select the pack via the in-game options overlay (**SELECT + START**), then **LANGUAGE** row. Packs are US-disc only (the game reads English from a US disc and Japanese from the JP disc natively). Full authoring and installation docs: docs/language-packs.md in the repo. Community packs are hosted separately by their authors (not in this project); one Spanish example: https://github.com/arcadematicas/traduccion-vandal-hearts-decompiled-espa-ol

build_steps: Extract the release ZIP to your desired location
Run git submodule update --init --recursive from the extracted folder
Run ./psxrecomp/tools/ci/build_emitters.sh
Place your disc image (CUE/BIN) in the disc/ folder
Run python3 psxrecomp/psxrecomp_cli.py generate --config game.toml --project-root . --disc disc/<your-disc-name>.cue
Run cmake -S . -B build-release -G Ninja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release
Run cmake --build build-release --target psx-runtime

games.game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

build_steps: Install Python 3.10 (add it to PATH during install), Git (x64 build) and Visual Studio Community 2022 with C++ development.
Clone the repo with submodules: git clone --recursive https://github.com/blawar/ooot.git, then cd ooot.
Put your ROM as baserom_original.z64 (or .n64) in roms\PAL_1.0\ (EUR PAL 1.0 retail) or roms\EUR_MQD\ (EUR Master Quest Debug).
Extract the assets: python setup.py -b PAL_1.0 (or python setup.py -b EUR_MQD).
Open OOT.sln from the vs folder, select Debug - Win32 or Release - Win32, right-click oot and click Build.

game_files.label: Ocarina of Time ROM (EUR PAL 1.0 retail)
game_files.description: The EUR PAL 1.0 retail ROM dumped from your own copy of the game. Needed to extract the game's assets before building.
game_files.notes: Use this OR the EUR Master Quest Debug ROM. Named baserom_original.z64 or baserom_original.n64. If the ROM's hash is not correct, setup.py won't extract the assets.

game_files.label: Ocarina of Time Master Quest Debug ROM (EUR)
game_files.description: The EUR Master Quest Debug ROM from your own copy. An alternative to the PAL 1.0 retail ROM for extracting the assets.
game_files.notes: Use this OR the PAL 1.0 retail ROM. Named baserom_original.z64 or baserom_original.n64. If the ROM's hash is not correct, setup.py won't extract the assets.

first_run: Build the project in Visual Studio (Win32 configuration) after extracting assets with setup.py.
Run the built oot program.
notes: Only the 32-bit x86/Win32 build is supported, with Visual Studio 2019 or newer.
You must use the ZAPD included with this repository, not the main ZAPD branch.
Clone with --recursive so the submodules come along.

Higher frame rates (30/60/120 FPS) are on the dev branch: git checkout dev, git pull origin dev, git submodule update --init --recursive, then rerun setup.py and build. In game, F7 goes back to 20 FPS and F8 steps up.
F9 toggles language (English, German, French).
Settings such as cheats, Owl prompts and control inversion are in config.json.
unsure: The README gives two different MD5s for the PAL 1.0 ROM (9526b263... near the top and c02c1d79... in the setup section); which one applies to .z64 vs .n64 isn't stated.

Where texture packs go isn't stated.

mods.notes: Ability to load high resolution GLideN64 texture packs such as oot-reloaded (https://evilgames.eu/texture-packs/oot-reloaded.htm).

game_files.description: A Redump-style dump of your own Dance Dance Revolution (Japan) disc, SLPM-86222: one .cue plus 40 .bin tracks (track 1 is data, 2-40 are the CDDA music). The setup-host asks for the disc and generates and compiles the game from it.
game_files.notes: Reference dump: Track 01 .bin is 14,935,200 bytes, md5 57d6ae6568a77409abfc94ba1d695b62. A wrong dump is refused. A different revision may still work, but the fixes were derived from this one.

first_run: Unzip ddr1st-0.4.0-windows-x64.zip and run it.
Point it at your own Dance Dance Revolution (Japan) .cue when asked; it generates and compiles the game on your machine (first run takes minutes).
Later runs start immediately; settings.toml is written beside the executable.
notes: The release is a setup-host, not a ready-made game: it builds the recompiled executable from your own disc.
The random hard-freeze is contained (not fully cured) by the runtime.
The README says publishing the setup-host zip had not yet been exercised from this repository when it was written.

game_files.label: PlayStation Doom disc image (.cue)
game_files.description: A disc image of PlayStation Doom from a disc you own, as a '.cue' file plus the disc data it describes. Final Doom, the Doom single level demo disc and GEC Master Edition Beta 3 or 4 are also supported.
game_files.notes: A valid .cue file must be provided before launching; it can be specified on launch with -cue <CUE_FILE_PATH>. All regions and editions of Doom and Final Doom are supported.

first_run: Make the AppImage executable and run it.
Provide your Doom .cue file (e.g. run with -cue <CUE_FILE_PATH>).
notes: Supported Linux versions are Debian 'Buster' based distros or later; others may work but are untested. PulseAudio is needed for sound.
One build runs both PlayStation Doom and Final Doom (all regions & editions) - supply whichever disc you own.
The Vulkan renderer (widescreen & high resolutions) needs a Vulkan 1.0 capable GPU (Metal on macOS); it is enabled by default where supported.
For the best audio quality set your audio device's sample rate to 44.1 kHz.
Link-cable multiplayer is emulated over TCP (default port 666 on Windows and macOS, 1666 on Linux) and needs a very low latency connection.
Pass -nolauncher (or any other command line argument) to skip the launcher.
This is a preview build (1.2.0-preview1); the latest stable release is releases/1.1.1.
unsure: The README does not say whether the launcher has a file picker for the .cue file; only the -cue command line argument is documented.

mods.notes: User mods are supplied in the form of a directory. Specify where the mod directory is located using launcher or via the `-datadir <MY_DIRECTORY_PATH>` command line argument. Extra IWADs can be added with `-file <WAD_FILE_PATH>`.

Logs and saves are under %APPDATA%\Godot\app_userdata\pokerecomp (Windows), ~/Library/Application Support/Godot/app_userdata/pokerecomp (macOS), ~/.local/share/godot/app_userdata/pokerecomp (Linux).
Pressing A, B, START and SELECT together resets to the save screen without saving.

game_files.label: Revenge of the Sith Xbox disc image (North America)
game_files.description: Your own disc image of Star Wars: Episode III - Revenge of the Sith for the original Xbox, North American release: an .iso (XISO or a full Redump-style image), or a .7z/.zip/.rar archive containing one. game_files.notes: The game's executable (default.xbe) must have MD5 6460ef37862de3af364a0563a0a18c4e - this is the hash of the executable inside the disc, not of the image file. Archives are unpacked with Windows' built-in tar (Windows 10 1803+); if that fails, unpack it yourself and choose the .iso. `swrots.exe --install <image>` skips the file dialog.

first_run: Unpack swrots.exe and core.dll from the zip into a folder of your choice, e.g. C:\Games\SWROTS.
Run swrots.exe. The first time, it asks for your disc image (.iso/.xiso, or a .7z/.zip/.rar containing one), checks it, copies the game files into GameData\ and adds a Start menu shortcut.
Play. Settings are in settings.ini and key bindings in controls.ini, both next to swrots.exe.
notes: Status: early development. Playable through level changes, restarts and saving, but not yet played through from start to finish; expect bugs.
Only the North American release is supported.
Requires 64-bit Windows 10 (1803) or newer and a Direct3D 9 capable graphics card (the port itself is a 32-bit program).
60 fps (FpsLimit=60) is experimental: some of the game's logic is timed for 30 fps.
The keyboard and the first controller are both player 1; two-player modes need two controllers. Controllers other than Xbox (XInput) and PlayStation need Steam Input or a similar translator.
To reinstall, delete the GameData folder; saves, settings and mods are kept.
unsure: The zip's exact contents beyond swrots.exe and core.dll are not listed.

mods.notes: Mods as loose files: replace textures, models and other game files without rebuilding archives. `mods\` overrides any disc file. Variables can be set at every start in `mods\vars_xbox.cfg` (`name=value`, one per line). Your own meshes go under `mods\meshes\chars\<folder>\` with their textures. Some limits: animations stored in a level's memory image (most `.bnm`) cannot be replaced by loose files yet, and loose text resources in folders the disc also has (e.g. `gameinfo\`) fail to load.

build_steps: Clone https://github.com/NagyD/SDLPoP.

Download the SDL2 and SDL2_image Visual C++ development packages (the *-VC.zip files) from https://github.com/libsdl-org/SDL/releases/latest and https://github.com/libsdl-org/SDL_image/releases/latest.
Copy the SDL2_image folder contents into the SDL2 folder so their DLLs and headers sit in the same place.
Open a command prompt and run Visual Studio's vcvarsall.bat with 'x64' as the parameter.
Set the SDL2 environment variable to that folder, e.g. set "SDL2=C:\libraries\SDL2-2.0.8".
Run build.bat in the src/ directory.
Add the SDL2 / SDL2_image DLL folder to PATH so the built executable can find them, then double-click prince.exe.

first_run: Double-click prince.exe (open a command line if you want to pass options such as 'full' for full screen).
Press Esc or Backspace for the in-game menu; Alt+Enter toggles full screen.
notes: The repository includes the game's data folder, so no separate game files are needed.
Alternatives to Visual Studio: Dev-C++ with the SDL2 MinGW libraries (open a .dev file and compile), MSVC with NMake (src/NMakefile), or CMake with MinGW-w64.
Prebuilt Windows versions are offered off GitHub at https://www.popot.org/get_the_games.php?game=SDLPoP.
Saves (SAV) and hall-of-fame (HOF) files go to the folder in SDLPOP_SAVE_PATH if that environment variable is set.
Gameplay bug fixes can be turned off with use_fixes_and_enhancements=false in SDLPoP.ini, or in the in-game settings menu (GAMEPLAY > Enhanced mode).
unsure: There are no GitHub releases; the README's compiled versions are hosted on popot.org.
The README's Visual Studio example uses 'x86'; that x64 builds work the same way is implied ('either x86 or x64') but not shown.

mods.notes: Since version 1.17, the game can also load from mod folders that have been placed in the "mods/" directory; only the files different from the original V1.0 data are required. Choose the mod by setting 'levelset' in SDLPoP.ini to the mod's folder name, or run `prince mod "Mod Name"`. Mods can also include a mod.ini and music in mods/<modname>/music. Example mod: https://forum.princed.org/viewtopic.php?f=73&t=3664 (alternate: https://www.popot.org/custom_levels.php?mod=0000153).

controller_notes: Joystick: left/right (for all-directional joystick movement, set joystick_only_horizontal to false in SDLPoP.ini)
If SDLPoP does not work correctly with your gamepad, it might help if you download gamecontrollerdb.txt and configure SDLPoP to use it.

build_steps: Install MSYS2 (msys2-x86_64-latest.exe) to C:\dev\msys64 and run it.
In the MSYS2 shell run: pacman -Syuu. Then open "MSYS2 MinGW 64-Bit" and run pacman -Syuu repeatedly until there are no more updates.
Install the toolchain: pacman -S --needed base-devel mingw-w64-i686-toolchain mingw-w64-x86_64-toolchain git subversion mercurial mingw-w64-i686-cmake mingw-w64-x86_64-cmake
Install dependencies: pacman -S mingw-w64-i686-glew mingw-w64-x86_64-glew mingw-w64-i686-SDL2 mingw-w64-x86_64-SDL2 python3
Clone the repository into a folder under C:\msys64\home\<username>\.
Copy your ROM into the repository root named baserom.us.z64.
cd tools/audiofile-0.3.6/ and run: autoreconf -i
Run: PATH=/mingw64/bin:/mingw32/bin:$PATH LIBS=-lstdc++ ./configure --disable-docs
Run: PATH=/mingw64/bin:/mingw32/bin:$PATH make
Run: mkdir ../lib, then cp libaudiofile/.libs/libaudiofile.a ../lib/ and cp libaudiofile/.libs/libaudiofile.la ../lib/
Edit tools/Makefile: change the line tabledesign_CFLAGS := -Wno-uninitialized -laudiofile to end with -lstdc++ (tabledesign_CFLAGS := -Wno-uninitialized -laudiofile -lstdc++).
cd .. and run: PATH=/mingw64/bin:/mingw32/bin:$PATH make
cd .. back to the repository root and run make, adding any options you want, e.g. PATH=/mingw32/bin:/mingw64/bin:$PATH make BETTERCAMERA=1 NODRAWINGDISTANCE=1
The .exe is produced under build\ (build/us_pc for the US version).

build_steps: Install Xcode Command Line Tools with: xcode-select --install
Install Homebrew and build dependencies with: brew install cmake ninja sdl2 ffmpeg glslang spirv-cross nlohmann-json python
Clone the repository: git clone https://github.com/Sean13128/disgaea-d2-recomp.git && cd disgaea-d2-recomp
Set up Python virtual environment: python3 -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/python -m pip install -r tools/requirements-lifts.txt
Bootstrap the SDK: ./tools/bootstrap_sdk.sh "$PWD/ps3recomp"
Decrypt your game executable with RPCS3 (File → Install Packages/Raps/Edats for 1.40 update and DLC, then Utilities → Decrypt PS3 Binaries on the EBOOT.BIN files)
Copy decrypted 1.40 EBOOT.elf to work/v140/EBOOT.elf (or work/EBOOT.elf for 1.00 version)
Generate lift code for version 1.40: PYTHON="$PWD/.venv/bin/python" ./tools/generate_lifts.sh --version 140

Configure CMake build: cmake -S port -B port/build -G Ninja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DPS3RECOMP_DIR=../ps3recomp -DD2_GAME_VERSION=140 -DPython3_EXECUTABLE="$PWD/.venv/bin/python" -DCMAKE_{C,CXX,OBJC,OBJCXX}_FLAGS=-I/opt/homebrew/include
Build the app: cmake --build port/build --target DisgaeaD2Dist
Run the app: open "port/dist/Disgaea D2.app"

first_run: Make the setup executable (chmod +x P.T.PC.Port.Setup-linux) and run it from a terminal.
Point it at your dump folder or fake PKG and at a destination folder; it copies the three game archives next to the port.
Start pt from the install folder (or the menu entry the setup creates).
Have a microphone ready for one part of the game, or set key = J under [voice] in pt.ini to use a key instead.
notes: Needs Linux x86-64 with glibc 2.38 or newer (Ubuntu 24.04, Debian 13, Fedora 39, current Arch and SteamOS) and a Vulkan 1.3 GPU/driver.
FSR, DLSS and XeSS upscalers are Windows-only and are left out of the Linux build.
On Steam Deck install from desktop mode and add pt as a non-Steam game.
Settings, save, pt.log and crash dumps go to ~/.local/share/pt-port/pt/.
The game checks the Releases page for a newer version at start; [network] check_updates = 0 in pt.ini turns that off.

game_files.notes: Put it in a disc folder next to launch.cmd or in %USERPROFILE%\Games\brave-fencer-musashi\disc. A file picker is offered when available, or set BFM_DISC to the .cue path.

first_run: Optional: verify the zip against SHA256SUMS (Get-FileHash ... -Algorithm SHA256).
Extract the zip to a folder you control, for example %USERPROFILE%\Games\bfm-port.
Put your .cue/.bin dump in a disc\ folder next to launch.cmd.
Run launch.cmd.
notes: Experimental hybrid port (compiled host code plus a CPU interpreter); the fully native port is still a goal. Whole-game completion and full graphics/audio fidelity are unverified.
This Windows x64 build is a test build that has been validated only under Wine, not on real Windows hardware. It is in the bfm-r41-3634893fe prerelease as well.
Dev menu is on by default (cheats off): F8 or Back/Select+Start opens it; BFM_DEV_MENU=0 turns it off.
Saves use a memory card file bfm_card0.mcd; the last run log is last-run.log in the same save folder.
unsure: General config.ini settings are not reliably loaded by r38 according to the README.
The README gives a SHA-256 only for the SLUS_007.26 executable inside the disc (in its architecture doc), not for the whole disc dump, so no disc hash is listed.
The README shows no screenshot or logo, so there is no artwork to link.

game_files.label: Halo: Combat Evolved Xbox disc image
game_files.description: A disc image (.xiso or .iso) of your own Xbox copy of Halo: Combat Evolved. All versions of the game work. On the first start the game asks for the disc image and extracts the maps/ folder from it.

game_files.label: Skate 2 Xbox 360 game files (extracted folder)
game_files.description: Your own extracted copy of the Xbox 360 game: a folder that directly contains default.xex and a data folder. An ISO or compressed archive must be extracted first. Import Game Files.cmd asks you to choose that folder, then copies and verifies it into the package's game folder.
game_files.notes: Supported revision: Xbox 360, Title ID 4541087F, Media ID 6ADB5821, executable version 0.0.0.2. Other revisions are rejected. The import needs about 6.8 GB for the supported file set. After import the package holds game/default.xex and game/data. The import is a one-time step and will not overwrite an existing game folder.

first_run: Extract the entire ZIP into a writable folder and keep all its files together (do not run from inside the ZIP).
Run Import Game Files.cmd and select your extracted Xbox 360 game folder containing default.xex and data. This is a one-time copy and verification step.
Connect your controller, then run Launch Skate 2.exe. If it asks for the Microsoft Visual C++ x64 Runtime, open Install Visual C++ Runtime.url, install it, and launch again.
Let the initial loading screen finish (it can be black for a while), then follow the in-game prompts.
notes: Requires Windows 10/11 x64, an x86-64-v2 processor and a Direct3D 12 GPU. Linux, macOS and Windows on ARM are not supported.

Use Launch Skate 2.exe each time so the graphics and frame-rate profile is applied; opening skate2.exe directly skips the launcher profile. Default is 2x quality with unlimited FPS; Launch Skate 2 - 1x Performance.cmd lowers GPU load.
Press F4 for PC settings and choose Save to config, then restart. Keep VSync enabled.
Known limits: true 21:9 and 32:9 ultrawide is not implemented; a controller is needed (USB DualSense works directly, other controllers are still being tested).
The ZIP excludes game, userdata, cache and skate2.toml, so extracting a newer release over an old install keeps your saves.

There is no networking support, and native mods will never work with Surreal Engine.
You can instead launch with: SurrealEngine [--url=<mapname>] [--engineversion=X] [Path to game folder].

game_files.notes: The setup checks first that speed.exe is one it can use and stops without changing anything if it is not. Your game folder is linked, not copied or changed.

first_run: Open the NFS-Most-Wanted-Native-Setup disk image. The app is not notarized, so the first time use the one-time Open Anyway step in System Settings > Privacy & Security.
Choose your game folder in the Setup app.
Click Build. About 10 minutes later on a recent Mac (longer on older ones) the game is in your Applications folder. An optional shader preparation step adds about 35 minutes.
notes: The app holds your copy of the game data; nothing it builds is meant to be shared.
Press F10 (Fn+F10 on a MacBook) for the settings menu.
Your profile folder is ~/Library/Application Support/NFS Most Wanted Native/; logs for bug reports are in its Logs folder. Back it up to keep your career.
Terminal alternative: ./setup.sh "/path/to/Need for Speed Most Wanted".
Optional: the Xbox 360 Stuff Pack textures and XenonEffects.tpk, if you already own them, are picked up from your game folder at build time.
unsure: Region requirement is not stated beyond Black Edition version 1.3.
Setup app dmg's exact first-run wording is in docs/GETTING_STARTED.md, which was only partly available.

required_tools: Libraries: liballegro5.2, liballegro-acodec5.2, liballegro-image5.2, libenet7, libfluidsynth3 (or libfluidsynth2), libmad0, libgl1 (Debian/Ubuntu); allegro5, allegro5-addon-acodec, allegro5-addon-image, enet, fluidsynth-libs (Fedora)

game_files.label: Dune II data files (*.PAK) - EU v1.07
game_files.description: The *.PAK data files from the EU v1.07 release of Dune II (Westwood Studios), from your own copy. data/FILELIST.TXT in the repo lists every needed file.
game_files.notes: The data folder next to the dunedynasty executable, or ~/.local/share/dunedynasty/data.

first_run: Install the required libraries (Debian/Ubuntu: sudo apt install liballegro5.2 liballegro-acodec5.2 liballegro-image5.2 libenet7 libfluidsynth3 libmad0 libgl1).
Extract dunedynasty-v1.6.4-linux-x86-64.zip.
Install/extract the download.
Copy your Dune II *.PAK files into the data folder (see game files).
Start Dune Dynasty. Display mode and resolution are changed in the Options and Extras menu; it starts in Fullscreen Window mode.
notes: Original Dune II game data files are required.
Fullscreen mode does not work on Linux and macOS currently (Fullscreen Window does).
Placing dunedynasty.cfg next to the executable runs in portable mode, keeping saves inside the install directory.
Multiplayer hosting needs UDP port 10700 forwarded.
Recommended optional mod: a normalized VOC.PAK by Tiddalick (https://www.moddb.com/games/dune-ii-the-building-of-a-dynasty/addons/vocpak-normalized).

The README calls the Flatpak package the recommended one for Linux (dunedynasty-v1.6.4-linux-amd64-flatpak.zip); with it, run the app once, then put the data files in ~/.var/app/io.github.gameflorist.dunedynasty/data/dunedynasty/data.
unsure: The full list of required PAK files is in data/FILELIST.TXT, which is not included here.
The exact executable name is not stated (README says 'the dunedynasty executable').
Whether the regular zip or the Flatpak zip is better for this app is a judgement call; the README recommends Flatpak.

mods.notes: Custom campaigns (Dune 2 eXtended, MrFlibble's Alternate Scenarios, Stefan Hendriks' Atreides campaign, Super Dune II) go in the existing subdirectories of the campaign directory, which sits in the same place as the data directory. Campaigns use META.INI, REGIONX.INI, SCENX001-022.INI, optional PROFILE.INI/HOUSE.INI, or a PAK file listed in META.INI. Links: http://forum.dune2k.com/topic/18360-dune-2-extended-project/ , http://arrakis.dune2k.com/downloads.html , http://forum.dune2k.com/topic/20065-super-dune-ii-classic/

game_files.description: Your own Breakdown (USA) Xbox disc image (.iso). The launcher asks for it on first start and builds the game from it on your computer.
game_files.notes: First time only: choose your disc image and press Continue. The build takes a few minutes and happens once (and once more after updating to a new release).

first_run: Extract the zip and keep the whole folder together; Breakdown.exe needs the tools folder beside it.
Run Breakdown.exe. If Windows warns about an unknown publisher, choose More info, then Run anyway.
Choose your disc image and press Continue; the one-time build takes a few minutes.
Press Play.
notes: Needs Windows 10 or 11 (64-bit), a Direct3D 11 graphics card and about 6 GB of free disk space for the one-time build. An Xbox-style controller is recommended.

Known issues in 0.2.2: in some rooms the background music plays a short repeating fragment (turning the BGM slider down silences it); loading after dying and choosing Retry can take a long time; some textures appear a moment late.
F11 or Alt+Enter switches full screen at any time. Brightness, Full screen and Saved games folder are set in the launcher Options.
The extracted game and build live in %LOCALAPPDATA%\BreakdownRecomp\work (delete it to rebuild); logs are in %LOCALAPPDATA%\BreakdownRecomp\logs.
The build is faster from a local disk than from a network share.

game_files.label: Sonic R PC game data folders
game_files.description: The data folders from an installed copy of the Sonic R PC release that you own: GENERAL, ISLAND, CITY, RUIN, FACTORY, EMERALD, AI, BIN and SOUND. They go into a single data directory, ideally the same folder as SONICR.EXE.
game_files.notes: SAVE and GHOST folders are created automatically on first play. If SONICR.EXE is not in the data directory, pass the data directory path as the first argument: SONICR.EXE C:\path\to\sonic-r-data.

game_files.label: Music tracks (optional)
game_files.description: Music tracks named by CD track number, track2 through track21, in a MUSIC folder in the data directory. Without them the game has no music.
game_files.notes: Files are named MUSIC/track2.<ext> through track21. The game looks for extensions in the order .adx, .son, .wav, .adp, .ogg, .mp3, .flac and the first match for a track wins.

first_run: Put SONICR.EXE inside the folder holding your Sonic R data folders (or pass that folder as the first argument).
Copy the contents of the repository's DATA folder into the data directory (BIN/OPTION/NET01.RAW and SOUND/SFX/REPLAY*.WAV); the README says to do this after laying out your data.
Optionally add a MUSIC folder with your track files.
Double-click SONICR.EXE, or run it with --fullscreen and/or --unlock.
notes: The release is a single statically linked x86-64 executable that bundles its libraries.

The README says the repository's DATA folder (NET01.RAW network icons and pre-split REPLAY*.WAV announcer sounds) is not in the original PC release and must be copied into your data directory; those files come from the source repository, not from the release asset.
Command-line options: --fullscreen, --unlock (unlock all characters and tracks), --host <ip>, --port <n> (default 7847), --username <name>.
Network play uses UDP port 7847 and everyone must run the same build and the same game data. Dreamcast cross-play is supported.
File and folder names must be uppercase.

games.game_title: Ultima Underworld: The Stygian Abyss (Underworld Revisited)

game_files.label: Ultima Underworld: The Stygian Abyss (GOG.com version)
game_files.description: Your own installation of Ultima Underworld 1 from GOG.com ("Ultima Underworld 1+2"). The game looks for it in the usual places; if it doesn't find it, it asks for the folder, which is the one that contains game.gog. Other releases (floppy, CD, other stores) are not supported.
game_files.notes: The choice is remembered and can be changed later in the main menu: Game > Game folder... On first start the game files are extracted from game.gog once into a local cache; nothing is written to the installation. The supported UW.EXE is 547,248 bytes.

game_files.label: Roland MT-32 / CM-32L ROMs (optional)
game_files.description: Optional: the control ROM and PCM ROM of your own Roland MT-32 or CM-32L, only needed if you want the MT-32 music. Not supplied with the game.
game_files.notes: Put them in the folder opened by the Open folder button in the Sound menu; the menu shows which ROMs were recognised.

first_run: Unpack the archive into a folder of its own.
Start UR.x86_64 (if Linux refuses to run it, run chmod +x UR.x86_64 in that folder once).
If the game doesn't find your GOG installation, choose the folder that contains game.gog.
notes: Only the GOG.com version of Ultima Underworld 1 is supported.
Save games are read from and written to the installation's UNDEROM1\SAVE1 to SAVE4, so they can be exchanged with the original game.
Shift+F2 switches between the original and modern control schemes; Tab opens the help window.
The package brings its own runtime; nothing else needs to be installed.
Linux needs 64-bit x86-64 with Vulkan or OpenGL 4; it is tested far less than the Windows version.
unsure: Accepted file extensions for the MT-32 ROMs aren't stated.
Ultima Underworld II support is only planned.

games.game_title: Eye of the Beholder III: Assault on Myth Drannor

game_files.label: Eye of the Beholder III game data (original DOS release)
game_files.description: The original game data from your own legal copy of Eye of the Beholder III, including EYE.RES. Thirdeye ships no game assets. The launcher picks the game folder.
game_files.notes: Use the launcher to pick the folder holding your game data. The game is detected from the .RES file.

first_run: Install Thirdeye from the download.
Start the Thirdeye launcher and pick the folder with your Eye of the Beholder III game data.
Set options (skip intro, sound, render scale) if you like, then launch.
notes: Thirdeye is a from-scratch reimplementation of the AESOP engine and runs the original game bytecode; saves stay DOS-compatible.
Handy launch switches: --scale=N, --skip-intro, --skip-menu, --load-save=N.
Press M in-game for an automap; WASD/QE work alongside the arrow keys and mouse.
A built-in OPL3 synth plays music with no soundfont setup.
unsure: The README doesn't say which edition, region or version of the game data is needed, and gives no checksums.
The README doesn't name the executable.
Dungeon Hack (HACK.RES + OPEN.RES) is only described as playable in the unreleased 0.90.0 changelog, so it is not listed as a game for the 0.89.0 release.

game_files.label: Road Trip disc image (USA, SLUS-20398)
game_files.description: Your own disc image of Road Trip (USA). The app copies the game files off it (about 512 MB) and builds the game on your device on first launch. It checks the image against the known good Redump dump and tells you if yours looks different.
game_files.notes: Docs list the supported image as 'Road Trip (USA).bin' / .cue with SHA-1 236b902a72580f43a480f18d232723a8676b02e5 (SYSTEM.CNF VER 1.02). Only the boot ELF's hash is checked, so any good dump of this version works.

first_run: Open the DMG and drag Road Trip to Applications.
If macOS says it can't be checked for malicious software, open System Settings > Privacy & Security and choose Open Anyway.
Open the app and pick your disc image when asked.
Wait for the one-time build (under a minute on an M-series Mac).
Play; Adventure and Quick Race are available from the title screen.
notes: Needs a Mac with Apple Silicon, macOS 13 or later, and Apple's Command Line Tools (the app offers to install them; or run xcode-select --install in Terminal).
Data lives in ~/Library/Application Support/RoadTripRecomp/ (disc/, game/, saves/, states/, settings.toml).
Don't share anything from the data folders except your own texture packs: they hold the game's files.

mods.notes: HD texture packs: turn on texture dumping (dump = true under [textures] in settings.toml), play, and the game saves every texture as PNG named by a hash of its pixels. Edit or upscale them (any size), keeping the file names, put them in a folder under textures/packs/ and pick it under Options > Texture pack. Packs are converted once on first use (ASTC on Android and Mac, BC7 on Windows).

first_run: Extract the archive.
Place the original GAMEMAPS.CK?, EGAGRAPH.CK? and AUDIO.CK? files and the matching 'data' files next to the omnispeak binary.
Run ./omnispeak from that directory (add /EPISODE 4, 5 or 6 to pick an episode).
notes: Omnispeak is one program for Commander Keen episodes 4, 5 and 6; you only need the files for the episode(s) you want to play.
Supported versions: Keen 4 v1.4 EGA, Keen 5 v1.4 EGA, Keen 6 v1.4 EGA and Keen 6 v1.5 EGA. Other versions (CGA, v1.0, retail FormGen / GT Interactive, the id Anthology Keen 6) will likely crash.
Command-line options include /EPISODE <episode>, /GAMEPATH <directory>, /USERPATH <directory>, /FULLSCREEN, /FILLED, /NOBORDER, /INTEGER, /NOJOYS, /NOCOPY.
F5 / F9 quicksave and quickload the final save slot; savegames from the DOS version are compatible.
unsure: The README refers to a 'data' directory to copy from but does not say whether the release archive contains it.
The 1.2preview release only has omnispeak-modding-preview.zip, which is not labelled for any OS, so v1.1 is used.

mods.notes: Omnispeak does not work with existing Keen mods unless designed for it. Data mods are an EPISODE.CKx-style variable file selected with the /EPISODE <episode.ckx> command-line argument; source mods require recompiling (doc/modding.md).

first_run: Extract PrinceOfPersia2-Windows.zip and run PoP2 Launcher.exe.
In the launcher, choose the game folder, fullscreen or window size, controller on or off, and optionally a start level.
Start the game. Desktop shortcut adds a desktop icon.
notes: pop2.exe is the original DOS PRINCE.EXE statically recompiled to C and linked with a small Windows runtime; the repository contains no game code, data or artwork.
Settings are saved in pop2.ini. Alt+Enter or F11 toggles fullscreen; F7 / F8 cycle display filter / view; Space skips the intro or shows time left; Esc pauses.
Sound emulates a Sound Blaster Pro using the port's own driver files; Sound=keep in pop2.ini uses the game's own setup instead.
Optional extra checkpoints (off by default): tick it in the launcher or set Checkpoints=1 in pop2.ini.
Cheat mode: pop2.exe MAKINIT, or pop2.exe MAKINIT LEVEL5 to start at level 5.

first_run: Mount or insert your Syndicate Plus CD or CD image and pick an install folder whose name ends with syndicatfx (for example c:\Program Files\syndicatfx).

game_files.label: Need for Speed: Carbon PC installation (version 1.4)
game_files.description: Your own installed copy of the PC game, version 1.4, on your Mac. The Setup app builds the playable app from this folder; it needs the folder containing an unwrapped NFSC.exe plus msvcr71.dll and msvcp71.dll.
game_files.notes: Choose or drop your game folder in the Setup app. The build checks the NFSC.exe SHA-256. The folder must also contain msvcr71.dll and msvcp71.dll.

first_run: Open the NFS-Carbon-Setup disk image. The app is not notarized: open it once, click Done, then go to System Settings > Privacy & Security and click Open Anyway.
Choose or drop your installed game folder (the one with NFSC.exe) in the Setup app.
Click Build. The first build takes a while (a one-time analysis of NFSC.exe); then the game is in your Applications folder.
notes: Game version 1.4 with an unwrapped NFSC.exe is required.
The Setup app holds no game files; it builds the game on your Mac from your copy. The built app contains your game data, so do not share it.
Press F10 (fn+F10 on a Mac keyboard) for the settings page; F11 shows a performance overlay.
Widescreen is supported at any resolution and aspect ratio in Options > Video.
Logs from each launch are in ~/Library/Application Support/NFS Carbon/Logs.
Terminal alternative: ./setup.sh "/path/to/Need for Speed - Carbon" (add --button-icons for controller icons).
unsure: The README does not name a region requirement beyond version 1.4.
The built app name is stated as Need for Speed Carbon in /Applications.

game_files.label: Shantae (USA) Game Boy Color ROM
game_files.description: The No-Intro dump of Shantae (USA) for Game Boy Color, from a cartridge you own. The launcher reads 'ROM verified' for it and enables PLAY only for that file; other dumps, other games and Shantae's other releases (World, Switch, Limited Run Games) read 'ROM not recognized' and do not start.
game_files.notes: The code was recompiled from that exact ROM.

first_run: Extract the download and run shantae.
The launcher asks for the ROM on the first start; pick your Shantae (USA) .gbc file.
Check the launcher says 'ROM verified' under the box art, then press PLAY.
notes: Boots as a Game Boy Advance by default, so the GBA Enhanced extras are on (title badge, Bandit Town Tinkerbat secret), while the palette loader stays on the original GBC colors.
Extras: expanded world view (choose an aspect ratio or Adaptive), no slowdown, reduced input lag, smoother movement, rewind, and RetroArch shader presets through librashader (Esc > Shader presets).
Shader choice and parameters are saved in runtime_prefs.ini.
The tar.gz folder runs from anywhere writable and keeps its state inside it. The binaries target glibc 2.28.
unsure: The README does not say where the launcher stores the picked ROM or the save files.
The README says only the USA No-Intro ROM is supported, but does not state the ROM's file extension.

game_files.label: Banjo-Tooie (USA) ROM
game_files.description: A .z64 dump of your own Banjo-Tooie (USA) cartridge. The launcher's Select ROM option reads it directly; there is no extraction step.
game_files.notes: Format is big-endian, unbyteswapped. Internal name BANJO TOOIE, cartridge ID NB7E. You only need to select it once.

first_run: Extract the archive.
Install the runtime libraries: libSDL2-2.0.so.0, libfreetype.so.6, libgtk-3.so.0, and a working Vulkan driver.
cd into the extracted BanjoTooieRecompiled folder and run ./run.sh.
On first launch, choose Select ROM and point it at your Banjo-Tooie (USA) .z64 ROM.
notes: Needs a GPU supporting Direct3D 12 (Shader Model 6) or Vulkan 1.2, and an SSE4.1-capable CPU.
The program must run with the working directory set to the folder containing assets/, otherwise it fails with 'Failed to load font face from assets\LatoLatin-Regular.ttf'.
--game bt skips the launcher and starts the game immediately, but a ROM must have been selected once.
Settings are stored in ~/.config/BanjoTooieRecompiled/.
The Linux build is newer and less exercised than the Windows one and has not been played through; Vulkan is required (no OpenGL backend).
unsure: The README does not name a save file location separately from the settings folder.
The README shows no screenshot or logo, so there is no artwork to link.

game_files.label: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2 (2009) installation with Multiplayer data
game_files.description: Your own installed copy of MW2 Multiplayer. IW4L reads the installation without patching or replacing its files. A Steam copy is found automatically; for an install outside Steam, create a Modern Warfare 2.lnk shortcut next to iw4l.exe pointing at your MW2 folder.
game_files.notes: The shortcut is created automatically when iw4l.exe finds MW2 in your Steam libraries. The build docs mention the Windows depot of the Steam copy (app 10190) as game data.

first_run: Download iw4l-windows.zip from Releases and extract it into an empty writable folder. The README states the archive password is t.me/contextrot.
Launch iw4l.exe. It finds MW2 in your Steam libraries and creates a Modern Warfare 2.lnk shortcut next to itself.
For an install outside Steam, create that Modern Warfare 2.lnk shortcut to your MW2 folder yourself.
For online play, put the .iw4l-server file you received from a server operator next to iw4l.exe.
notes: Experimental: gameplay is incomplete, and APIs, configuration, caches and the wire protocol change between commits; multiplayer peers must run the same build.
The release zip is password protected (password given in the README).
Caches, demos and logs go under iw4l-artifacts/.
The README says the whole project is written by an LLM.
unsure: docs/WINDOWS.md (the Windows guide) was not included in the text, so details of the portable folder layout are unknown.

game_files.label: Def Jam: Fight for NY Xbox dump (USA)
game_files.description: Your own dump of the USA Xbox version: a disc image (ISO/XISO) or an extracted folder, matching the project's dump manifest. The setup tool checks it, then translates and compiles the game on your machine. PS2 and GameCube copies cannot be used.
game_files.notes: The setup wizard asks for the dump; nothing from it is uploaded or bundled. Verified against config/dump-manifest.json (default.xbe).

first_run: Unpack the tar.gz and open DefJamSetup.sh (on Steam Deck Desktop Mode, double-click it and choose Execute).
Choose your Xbox dump, an install folder and a data folder in the wizard; it checks the dump, then translates and compiles the game locally.
Start the game from the shortcut; a launcher window opens with display, controller and key settings and a Play button (F1 opens the same settings in game).
notes: Only the USA Xbox version matching the dump manifest is supported.
Early release: Windows is playable, a full Story playthrough has not been verified, and the picture is 4:3 (true 16:9 is planned).
Profiles and settings.ini live in your data folder and survive updates and repairs.
A computer with no compiler (like the Steam Deck) builds in a container that setup fetches once (about 1 GB), so the first install needs internet.
Setup offers Add to Steam so the game starts from Gaming Mode.
unsure: The README gives no hash or size for the dump in the text provided (the manifest is config/dump-manifest.json).
The name of the final game executable is not stated; setup creates shortcuts.
Exact disc-image extensions and the settings.ini key names are in linked docs not included here.

mods.notes: Optional 4x HD texture packs are generated on your machine from your own dump (Windows and macOS); see docs/hd-textures.md. No other mod folder is described.

games.game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Oracle of Ages

game_files.label: Oracle of Ages ROM (USA/Australia)
game_files.description: A ROM dump of the cartridge you own. The Oracles hashes are verified at launch; a different revision gets a warning.
game_files.notes: Drop the ROM into the roms/ folder next to the binary. Either game alone is fine.

first_run: Unzip the download.
Put your ROM (tlozooa.gbc) into the roms/ folder next to the binary.
Run epoch (double-click works) to open the launcher.
notes: One binary plays both Oracle games; either ROM alone is fine, and other Game Boy / Game Boy Color ROMs in roms/ show up too.
No game code is included in the binaries; the ROM is read at runtime.
Voxel mode is off by default (F3 cycles it); F5/F8 save and load states; Esc or F10 opens the menu.
Mods that change the ROM size are skipped.

mods.notes: Mods are applied to the extracted ROM before the cart boots. One directory per mod under mods/, each with a required manifest.json and an IPS or BPS patch named by the manifest. A patch that changes the ROM's size can't work. BPS patches carry a source checksum; one built for a different revision is rejected.

game_files.label: Parasite Eve (USA) Disc 1, BIN/CUE
game_files.description: A raw Redump-style BIN/CUE image of Parasite Eve (USA) Disc 1: one .bin of 495,531,120 bytes next to its .cue. An .iso or .chd does not work directly. Disc 2, other regions and modified images are refused.
game_files.notes: Put the .bin and .cue together in a folder of their own, for example ~/Games/parasite-eve/disc/Parasite Eve (USA) (Disc 1).bin and .cue, then pass that folder (or the .bin or .cue) to the launcher as an argument, or save the path once with: mkdir -p ~/.config/parasite-eve-port && echo "disc1=$HOME/Games/parasite-eve/disc" > ~/.config/parasite-eve-port/config. Nothing needs to be extracted; the port reads the image directly and checks it on start. A .chd can be converted with chdman extractcd (from MAME). No BIOS is needed. The hashes are those the project recorded from its own dump; its Redump cross-check is marked pending.

first_run: Unpack the tar.gz into ~/Games (for example: mkdir -p ~/Games && tar xzf ~/Downloads/<the .tar.gz> -C ~/Games).
Put your Disc 1 .bin and .cue together in a folder of their own, for example ~/Games/parasite-eve/disc.

Run the parasite-eve launcher inside the unpacked folder with the disc folder as its argument (it also accepts the .bin or .cue), or save the disc path once in ~/.config/parasite-eve-port/config as disc1=<folder> and run it with no argument.
It starts fullscreen; set PE_WINDOWED=1 for a window.
notes: Native Linux x86-64 build, not an emulator; no BIOS is needed. Requires glibc 2.34 or newer (2021-or-later distribution, including SteamOS 3 and Bazzite), an X display (XWayland is fine) and libpulse-simple.so.0 for sound.

This native-only build runs only native C: a function that is not ported yet stops the game with a CPU_BOUNDARY/REFUSED message. The README says it plays Day 1 through the opening of Day 2, is untested by hand past Day 1 and has not been played on real hardware; the hardware-tested Day 1 build is the day1-r5 release.
Memory card saves go to ~/.local/share/parasite-eve-port/memcard1.mcd. Logs are written to ~/.local/state/parasite-eve-port/logs/.
Steam Deck / Bazzite: save the disc path once, add the parasite-eve launcher to Steam as a Non-Steam Game, and use the default Gamepad layout.
Dev menu (cheats, off unless pressed): F1 help, F2 god mode, F3 infinite ammo, F4 win battle, F5 key items, F6 fast-forward, F8 warp menu.
unsure: The how-to-play instructions are written for the day1-r5 release; the folder name the native-only tarball unpacks to is not stated (the README example for r5 is parasite-eve-day1-day1-r5-16a267b1).

Put your NHL 14 disc image (.iso) in that folder.

The first start takes a few minutes, once: it checks the disc, extracts it into game/ and translates the shaders for your GPU. After that it starts straight away.
notes: Needs a GPU with Vulkan 1.2 on a current driver, 8 GB RAM (16 GB recommended), 7 GB disk, and a 64-bit x86 CPU with SSE4.2 and 4 cores. Windows 10/11 64-bit.

F1 opens settings, F3 shows frame times, the backtick key opens a console. Any controller SDL recognises works; without one the keyboard stands in for an Xbox pad.
Offline modes only: Hockey Ultimate Team, online play and the 2013-14 Moments Live downloads needed EA's servers, which are gone.

build_steps: git clone https://github.com/PatrikScully/OpenSpidey.git, then cd OpenSpidey
In the MSYS2 MINGW32 shell: pacman -S --needed mingw-w64-i686-gcc mingw-w64-i686-cmake mingw-w64-i686-zlib mingw-w64-i686-pkgconf mingw-w64-i686-ninja
Extract the pinned SDL3 MinGW development archive named in packaging/versions.json and set PKG_CONFIG_PATH to the lib/pkgconfig directory in its i686-w64-mingw32 prefix
cmake -S . -B out-native-win -G Ninja -DSPIDEY_STANDALONE=ON -DSPIDEY_BACKEND=sdl3 -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=RelWithDebInfo
cmake --build out-native-win -j8
Keep SDL3.dll and the MinGW runtime DLLs beside spider.exe, or run it from the configured MSYS2 environment
required_tools: MSYS2 MINGW32 (32-bit GCC, CMake, zlib, pkgconf, Ninja)

game_files.label: Import Tuner Challenge game files (extracted from your Xbox 360 backup)
game_files.description: The game's files extracted from a backup of your own copy into a folder. The release zip is extracted into this same folder, next to default.xex.
game_files.notes: The README says to extract the game's files from your backup into a folder, then extract the release zip's files into that folder next to default.xex, and run ./run.sh from there. It does not say how to extract the backup.

first_run: Extract the game's files from your backup into a folder.
Extract the release zip's files into that same folder, next to default.xex.
Run ./run.sh from that folder.
notes: Needs Linux on a 64-bit x86 CPU with SSE4.2 and a GPU with Vulkan support.

./run.sh turns frame interpolation on (up to 144 fps in races, no logging). Options: --max_fps=N (0 is unlimited), --no-interpolation (original 30 fps), --skip_intro (can occasionally hang at startup; restart if so).
./run-debug.sh is the same as run.sh with logging written to logs/; attach the newest log when reporting a problem.
Game logic still runs at 30 Hz; if your machine cannot keep up, the game runs in slow motion.

Known limitations: only races are interpolated, in-game movies are not shown, colors are slightly lighter than on the console, and it is tested on only a small number of Linux machines. The native Vulkan renderer is work in progress and still quite slow.
A Windows build is planned for later.

game_files.label: Majora's Mask 3D decrypted ROM (USA v1.1)
game_files.description: Your own decrypted dump of The Legend of Zelda: Majora's Mask 3D, USA v1.1, as .3ds or .cci. Setup extracts it, translates the code and builds the game module on your PC; nothing of the game is downloaded or distributed.
game_files.notes: Put the ROM in the folder you extracted the release into (or pass its path to the setup script). Setup checks the code.bin hash of the supported version.

first_run: Extract MM3D-PC-Windows.zip to a short, writable folder such as C:\Games\MM3D (not Program Files).
Put your ROM in that folder (or drag it onto Setup.bat), then run Setup.bat. If Windows warns about an unsigned script choose More info > Run anyway.
Wait 10-40 minutes; the log is logs\setup.log.
Play with Play.bat.
notes: Setup runs once and takes 10-40 minutes, downloading a compiler and checking each download against a pinned SHA-256; it needs an Internet connection the first time.
About 4 GB of disk space, 8 GB of RAM and a GPU with Vulkan 1.2 and current drivers are required.
At the end of setup a shader tour opens and closes game windows by itself (15-40 minutes). You can close it and finish later with BuildShaders.bat / ./BuildShaders.sh.
The README warns that performance may be bad right now (stutter, frame drops) and that the author may not keep working on the project.
Updating: extract the new release into a new folder and run Setup again with the same ROM; then copy data/savedata, data/textures and (to keep settings) data/config from the old folder.
F1 opens the settings menu, F11 toggles fullscreen. Button prompt styles (Xbox, DualShock, Nintendo, SNES, 3DS) are chosen in F1 > Button style.
Setup downloads HardDanX's Omni UI button textures from GameBanana.
Requires Windows 10/11 x64.
unsure: The README does not publish the code.bin hash it checks.
The README does not name the game executable; Play.bat / Play.sh launches the game after Setup.

mods.notes: Texture packs (Azahar/Citra format, e.g. Henriko Magnifico's MM3D 4K pack): copy the contents of the pack's title folder into data/textures. Sub-folders are fine, and packs with or without pack.json both work. With enough RAM, turn on F1 > Textures > Preload custom textures and raise Texture memory (the 4K pack needs about 6.5 GB).

game_files.label: Go Go Ackman ROM (Japan)
game_files.description: A ROM of your own copy of the Japanese release (LoROM). An optional 512-byte copier header is normalized during verification; a different revision is not supported.
game_files.notes: If the configured ROM cannot be found, the native file picker opens before the emulation core starts. The README suggests placing the ROM in the rom/ folder for convenient selection. Verified size is 1,310,720 bytes without a copier header.

first_run: Extract the zip.
Launch AckmanRecomp.exe.
If it cannot find the ROM, the file picker opens: choose your Japanese Go Go Ackman ROM (or put it in the rom folder first).
notes: Press Esc for the in-game menu (File, Game, Graphics, Audio, Controls, Hotkeys, Mods, Shaders); opening it pauses the game.
U switches between widescreen and 4:3 in real time; Tab is turbo, R is rewind, F12 takes a screenshot.
Up to 10 savestate slots plus autosave; run-ahead, rumble and shaders (.glsl/.glslp in the shaders folder, with the OpenGL output method) are supported.

The English translation by Ackman Translations and the Brazilian Portuguese translation by E2P Traducoes can be converted from their .ips files in the Mods tab (convert, then move to Active; one at a time).
Settings, saves and mods live in folders next to the program (rom, saves, mods, shaders, screenshots) and a single config.ini.
unsure: MSU-1 support is described as untested.
Translation conversion is automated and not guaranteed for every .ips file.

mods.notes: Native snesrecomp .snesmod packages and MSU-1 packages go in the mods folder. In the Mods tab, use Load .ips file to convert a supported patch into a native package, then transfer it to Active. game_files.label: Pokémon SoulSilver (US) ROM
game_files.description: Your own dump of Pokémon SoulSilver (US) as a .nds file, dumped from your cartridge. Nothing of the game is in the repository or its releases; the setup program checks that the ROM is the right game and then builds the game from it on your machine.
game_files.notes: Choose the ROM in the setup window, or pass it with --rom your-rom.nds.

first_run: Make the setup program executable (chmod +x ssrecomp-setup-linux-x86_64) and start it.
Choose your ROM, press Build, wait (the first build takes 20-40 minutes), then press Play.
notes: The download is a setup program, not the game itself: it unpacks the project source, then builds the game from your ROM on your machine. The first build takes 20 to 40 minutes.
The save file and settings are kept in the setup program's data folder. Updating: the setup window shows whether a newer release is out; press Update, then press Build once to rebuild.
Portable mode: put an empty file named portable.txt next to the setup program; everything then goes into an ssrecomp-data folder beside it.
The default single-screen view shows one picture with the touch-screen buttons laid out around it; play with a controller or keyboard (pause menu: Esc, or Start + Select).
Made with heavy use of AI (per the README); expect bugs.

Needs build tools: on Ubuntu/Debian/Mint run sudo apt install cmake ninja-build g++ pkg-config libsdl2-dev libpng-dev zlib1g-dev (other distributions have equivalent commands in the README). On immutable Linux such as Bazzite or SteamOS, run it in a distrobox container. On Steam Deck, add run.sh to Steam as a non-Steam game.
unsure: Windows gameplay and the Windows build are described as untested.
macOS support is marked experimental; the Mac setup download is described as available only 'when available'.
The README does not give a checksum or exact size for the ROM.
The name of the program that launches the finished game is not stated for the release builds (run.sh is mentioned for source checkouts).

game_files.label: Shinobi III ROM (USA, Europe, or Japan/Korea)
game_files.description: A dump of your own original 1993 retail cartridge. Must be exactly 1,048,576 bytes, plain big-endian .bin with no copier header and no SMD interleaving. Modified, prototype, zipped and interleaved images are rejected.
game_files.notes: Choose the ROM in the startup file picker; the game remembers its location. Alternatively name the dump shinobi3_us.bin and put it beside the executable (beside the .app on macOS), pass --rom "/path/to/your/game.bin", or set the NINJA_MASTER_ROM environment variable. Supported dumps: USA Shinobi III MPR-15674-F, Europe Shinobi III MPR-15798 T57, Japan / Korea The Super Shinobi II.

first_run: Install your distribution's SDL2 runtime first.
Extract the tar.gz and run play.sh.
Choose your ROM in the startup file picker (the game remembers it).
Press Enter, select NEW GAME, and press Enter again.
notes: No ROM or original game assets are included in the download.
Startup reports the detected release and rejects modified, prototype, zipped and interleaved images. Filenames do not establish compatibility.
The three hash pairs listed are for the USA, Europe and Japan / Korea dumps in that order (CRC32 then SHA-1 each); any one matching dump is enough.

Settings and saves live in the user configuration folder: %APPDATA%\ninja-master\ on Windows, ~/Library/Application Support/ninja-master/ on macOS, $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/ninja-master/ or ~/.config/ninja-master/ on Linux.
Each download has a .sha256 file for verifying its checksum.
Linux builds are tested on Ubuntu 24.04 and Fedora; older distributions may need newer system libraries. Full playthroughs were tested on Linux and Windows.

game_files.label: Minecraft: Java Edition 26.3 installation
game_files.description: Your own copy of Minecraft: Java Edition installed with the official launcher and with 26.3 played once. Horizon reads versions/26.3/, libraries/ and assets/ from the official launcher's game directory (~/.minecraft on Linux) and prepares its resources from them, verified against checksums in research-lock.json.
game_files.notes: Nothing is copied by hand. If your Minecraft folder is somewhere else, the developer instructions use --minecraft-dir or HORIZON_MINECRAFT_DIR; the Horizon launcher shows the Minecraft folder in its window. The README says the game is meant to be installed through the Horizon launcher.

game_files.label: Minecraft 26.3 server jar (first-time preparation only)
game_files.description: The 26.3 server jar, taken from the downloads.server.url in your official launcher's versions/26.3/26.3.json (or from minecraft.net/download/server while 26.3 is the current release). It is only needed the first time resources are prepared.
game_files.notes: The documented developer command passes it with --server-jar or the HORIZON_SERVER_JAR environment variable; the docs provided do not say how the launcher asks for it.

first_run: Install Minecraft: Java Edition with the official launcher and play 26.3 once.
Install Python 3.10+ and a Java 25 JDK for the one-time resource preparation.
Get Horizon through the Horizon launcher (playhorizon.dev), which installs the build and prepares its resources from your copy of Minecraft.
Start the client from the launcher.
notes: Horizon is a Rust rewrite of Minecraft: Java Edition 26.3; it contains no Minecraft code, assets or data and never downloads them. It builds its resources from your own copy, and those prepared resources are derived from the game: never share them.

The README says Horizon is downloaded only through the Horizon launcher (playhorizon.dev, or the newest launcher-v* release). The launcher installs and updates the game, prepares its resources from your copy of Minecraft, starts the client or a dedicated server, and updates itself.
One-time resource preparation needs Python 3.10 or newer and Java 25 (a JDK, e.g. Eclipse Temurin 25).
Known issues: online-mode servers (Mojang's session servers) are not supported; skins served over https show the default skin unless already cached.
Options -> Interface -> Menu style -> Classic switches to the vanilla-style menus. horizon-ctl (a command line and MCP server for scripts) ships beside the game in every release folder.
Any Apple Silicon Mac works.
unsure: The README says to install through the Horizon launcher; whether the plain game archive can prepare its own resources without the launcher is not described in the provided docs.
The executable name inside the archive is not stated.
How the launcher asks for the Minecraft folder and the server jar is not described in the provided docs.

first_run: Install Java 21 (JDK or JRE, for example Temurin 21) so that java is on your PATH.

notes: No game files are needed from you: this is a port of a 2005 Nokia J2ME rally game with its own 3D engine, and the game resources are part of the project.

Click Play.

game_files.label: Pokemon Mystery Dungeon - Red Rescue Team ROM (USA, Australia)
game_files.description: A dump of your own cartridge, as an unzipped .gba file. Any other revision or region is refused because the recompiled code is tied to this exact ROM.
game_files.notes: File names do not matter, the app recognizes files by content. It also searches anywhere in ~/Downloads or your home folder. The ROM is only read, never copied or modified. It must not be zipped.

game_files.label: GBA BIOS
game_files.description: A dump of your own Game Boy Advance BIOS, 16 KB. The game is compiled from the ROM and the BIOS on your machine.
game_files.notes: File names do not matter for detection (recognized by content), but the expected dump is gba_bios.bin. It is also found anywhere in ~/Downloads or your home folder.

first_run: Install the Flatpak: flatpak install --user ./PMDRedRescueTeamRecomp-linux-x86_64-*.flatpak (the first install also fetches the Freedesktop SDK, about 1 GB, which provides the compiler).
Put the ROM and the BIOS in ~/Emulation/roms/gba/ and ~/Emulation/bios/ (or anywhere in ~/Downloads or your home folder).
Launch PMD Red Rescue Team Recomp; both files should show as Verified.
Press Build and play. The game compiles once (about 1 minute on a desktop PC, 5 to 8 minutes on a Steam Deck); later launches start the game directly.
notes: Preview: the game is playable, but code the recompiler has not reached runs through a built-in interpreter the first time, is recompiled on the fly and cached, so it gets faster the more it is played.
Everything the app writes is in ~/.var/app/io.github.roblittiere.PMDRedRescueTeamRecomp/data/PMDRedRescueTeamRecomp/ (compiled game in src/, saves and save states in saves/, build log build.log).

Update by installing the new release; the next launch recompiles once, usually in seconds. Uninstall with flatpak uninstall io.github.roblittiere.PMDRedRescueTeamRecomp and delete the data folder to remove saves too.

Steam Deck: after installing in Desktop Mode (from Konsole), add it via Steam > Games > Add a Non-Steam Game to My Library. In Gaming Mode the first-launch screen works with the controller alone. Steam Deck support is not yet validated on hardware.

The Choose file button does nothing inside the Flatpak sandbox yet; move the files into one of the searched folders. Run flatpak run io.github.roblittiere.PMDRedRescueTeamRecomp --scan to see what the search finds.
Hotkeys: F11 fullscreen, P pause, 1 / 2 held rewind / fast-forward, F1-F9 load state, Shift+F1-F9 save state, Escape settings menu.

Run it, choose your FIFA Street ISO and an empty folder, then press INSTALL ReStreet.

notes: The v1.3 release is the last full installer. To update an earlier version, select the folder that contains Game and GameData; no ISO is needed and saves and settings are kept.
FPS counter: Home. Exit prompt: hold START and press B (Xbox layout) or START and Circle (PlayStation layout).
Launch without the launcher window with FifaStreetLauncher.exe --play.
Tested mostly on one AMD GPU; NVIDIA and Intel graphics and Windows 10 are not tested. Other ISO regions or revisions are untested; only builds matching the three verified module hashes are accepted.

build_steps: Clone recursively: git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/sergiomanzur/noble-archimedes.git, then apply the supplied runtime patch once to the pinned submodule (git -C tools/PS2Recomp apply --check ../../patches/ps2recomp-progress.patch, then git -C tools/PS2Recomp apply ../../patches/ps2recomp-progress.patch).

Place your disc image at the repository root as 'Castlevania - Curse of Darkness (USA).iso' and extract SLUS_211.68 from it to extracted/SLUS_211.68 (BUILDING.md has a short Python snippet using tools/ps2_iso_reader.py).

Fetch dependencies and build PS2Recomp: python tools/PS2Recomp/ps2xRuntime/scripts/fetch_parallel_gs.py, then cmake -S tools/PS2Recomp -B tools/PS2Recomp/build -G Ninja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=gcc -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=g++ -DPS2X_BUILD_STUDIO=OFF -DPS2X_BUILD_TEST=OFF -DPS2X_ENABLE_PGS=ON, then cmake --build tools/PS2Recomp/build --target ps2_recomp ps2_runtime ps2_iop --parallel 2.

Generate the guest C++ locally: run the built ps2_recomp.exe with cvcod_ps2recomp_config.toml, then python tools/generate_stub_registry.py, python tools/optimize_register_functions.py and python tools/generate_entry_chunk.py.
Build and link: python tools/build_recomp_chunks.py --jobs 2 (about 20 minutes on the author's machine), then python tools/link_noble_archimedes.py.

Copy the required FFmpeg, window and compiler-runtime DLLs beside NobleArchimedes.exe (no DLL bundle is provided), keep the ISO and extracted/SLUS_211.68 beside it, set PS2_GS_BACKEND=pgs and run NobleArchimedes.exe.
