game_files.description: The Xbox 360 STFS package of the game from your own console: a file with a 40-character hexadecimal name, stored on the console's drive under Content/0000000000000000/58410975/000D0000/ (58410975 is the game's title ID). game_files.notes: The package is unpacked automatically the first time the game starts (a few seconds), then a small menu patch is applied to data0.big and data0.bh; afterwards you can delete the package. notes: Both archives are portable: unpack anywhere, nothing is installed, and settings stay in that folder. nhl3on3.toml (your settings) and logs/ are created beside the game.
Needs a 64-bit CPU with AVX2 (Intel Haswell 2013 / AMD Ryzen or newer) and a controller is recommended (anything SDL supports).
Online play: turn it on in the launcher's Online tab and set a gamertag. Every player needs the same release version. Up to three skaters and a goalie per team.
F11 or Alt+Enter toggles fullscreen in game. Extra launcher arguments are passed to the game as-is (for example --log_fps=true).
Needs a 2023-or-newer distribution (glibc 2.38 and libstdc++ from GCC 13: Ubuntu 24.04, Debian 13, Fedora 39, Arch or newer), a Vulkan driver (Mesa or NVIDIA) and an X11 or Wayland desktop.
If the launcher shows a Vulkan error, install your GPU's Vulkan driver (for example mesa-vulkan-drivers on Debian/Ubuntu); you can still edit nhl3on3.toml by hand and run ./nhl3on3.

game_files.label: NFL Head Coach 09 disc image
game_files.description: An .iso image of your own NFL Head Coach 09 (Xbox 360) disc. The setup wizard checks it is the right game, imports the game's executable from it, recompiles it on your PC and builds HC09.exe. The image stays where it is: the game reads its data from it while you play.
game_files.notes: The setup wizard asks for the image. Running setup again with the same folder is how you change the disc image later. The path is stored as IsoPath in hc09.ini in the install folder.

first_run: Download and run HC09Setup.exe.
The wizard checks for Visual Studio (with the C++ workloads listed) and Git for Windows.
Choose an install folder (a short path such as C:\Games\HC09Recomp is best) and your NFL Head Coach 09 .iso.
Choose whether to enable automatic update checks; the game then checks the latest release at each start and asks before downloading and rebuilding.
Wait for the wizard to download the source, XenonRecomp and FFmpeg (about 1 GB) and to recompile and build HC09.exe (10 to 20 minutes); it then adds a Start menu shortcut.
notes: HC09Setup.exe contains no game code. The game is built on your PC because the recompiled executable is derived from the game's own code, which the project does not distribute.
Running setup again and choosing the same folder updates the installation to the latest release and keeps your saves. The setup log is %TEMP%\HC09Setup.log.
Settings live in hc09.ini in the install folder (IsoPath, AutoUpdate).
F11 or Alt+Enter toggles borderless fullscreen; the picture keeps its 16:9 shape. Set HC09_RESOLUTION_SCALE=2 (up to 4) to render at a multiple of 1280x720.

Menus and in-game screens run at about 30-35 fps. Known issues: the video and LED boards at the Colts' stadium (Lucas Oil) show a flat flickering slab (the game's own missing data); predicated tiling and some MSAA cases are approximated.
Saves are folders under build/userdata/content/<type>/ in the install folder.

game_files.label: Game data: arcade ROM set, Arcade Archives main, or X68000 Disk 1 (one is enough)
game_files.description: ONE source from your own copy of the game, copied into the data/ folder next to the game. (1) Arcade: MAME's flstory set, unzipped, files loose in data/ (the older flstoryo set also works); the files used are cpu-a45.15 to .17, vid-a45.06 to .09, vid-a45.18 to .21 and a45-20.mcu, and the MCU dump is required. (2) Nintendo Switch Arcade Archives: copy the ExeFS file named main into data/ and Copernicus extracts the ROMs on first start. (3) X68000: Disk 1 as .hdm or .dim, or the loose files FS.X, BGCHR.DAT and SPCHR.DAT (plus FLS_TTL.DAT for the boot picture).
game_files.notes: ROMs are recognised by their contents (CRC32), not their names, so renamed files and merged dumps work. If both arcade and X68000 files are present the arcade files are used; start with --source x68k to use the X68000 disk. Disk 2 (the save disk) is not needed. The README does not print the CRC32 values. data/README.txt in the download has the same list. The PlayStation 4 Arcade Archives release is untested.

first_run: Extract the zip.
Copy your game data into the data/ folder next to the game.
Start the game; it plays like the arcade by default (GAME OPTIONS > BEHAVIOUR switches to the X68000 behaviour).
notes: Copernicus is a clean reimplementation of The Fairyland Story in the DragonRuby engine, not a decompilation or an emulator. The README says it was heavily written with AI (Claude) and checked frame by frame against MAME and a real PCB.
No game data is distributed in the repository. Release builds do contain the game audio, which the README says is necessary for it to run, but the game still needs your data to work.

game_files.label: Burnout 3: Takedown disc (North America, NTSC-U)
game_files.description: A copy of your own North America (NTSC-U) retail Xbox disc: an .iso in XISO layout, a full disc image with the video partition first, or a folder with the extracted files. Takedawn copies the game data into your user folder (about 2.5 GB, 3 GB free space needed) and checks every one of the 716 files against a list of known sizes and SHA-256 sums.
game_files.notes: A setup window opens on first start while the game data is missing; choose the disc image or folder, or drop it on the window, then press Install. PAL and Japanese discs and patched files are refused. After install you can delete the disc image.

first_run: Run the setup program (not code signed: on "Windows protected your PC" click More info, then Run anyway). It installs for your user account only, in %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Takedawn.
Start Takedawn from the Start menu; in the setup window choose your disc image or folder, press Install, then Play.
notes: Only the North America (NTSC-U) retail Xbox disc is supported. The setup recognises it by the SHA-256 of its default.xbe: 9f497acd82adb8edfb72cc31aeeb35010b45d32b13a3f1fc6540717ff24d13f9 (this is the hash of that file inside the disc, not of the disc image).
The setup window checks the disc and installs the game data; press Play afterwards. The first Play runs a shader pre-build (the "Prepare graphics" box, ticked by default).
Settings open with Back and Start together on a controller, or F1 on a keyboard; changes are saved to settings.toml in the save folder.
For full 60 fps you need about a Steam Deck's power; below 60 fps the whole game runs slower.
Updates are manual: install the new version over the old one; saves, settings and installed game data stay.
Game data goes to %LOCALAPPDATA%\Takedawn\Game and saves to %APPDATA%\Takedawn. Needs 64-bit Windows 10 or newer and a Vulkan 1.3 graphics driver.

game_files.label: Haze disc-decrypted ISO (USA, BLUS30094)
game_files.description: A disc-decrypted image of your own USA disc of Haze, BLUS30094, disc version 01.02 / application version 01.00. The installer extracts it and decrypts the executable on your PC.
game_files.notes: The tested image is named Haze (USA) (En,Fr,Es).iso. Setup also checks the disc metadata and executable hashes; other regions, encrypted raw dumps and updated executables are unsupported.

first_run: Run HazeRecomp-0.1.11-Setup.exe (optionally compare its hash with SHA256SUMS.txt from the same release).
Select your disc-decrypted Haze USA ISO and click Install.
The installer downloads the verified RPCS3 helper and Sony firmware, extracts your disc, decrypts its executable and prepares the firmware (internet access needed).
When preparation finishes, click Play Haze. Later, start Haze Recomp from the Start menu.
notes: The installer downloads Sony firmware and an RPCS3 helper itself; no separate tools are needed. It needs at least 12 GB free, Windows x64, SSE4.1 and D3D12 graphics support.
The default installation folder is %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Haze Recomp. The first launch installs about 4 GB of game data.
Experimental: full campaign completion is not validated. Co-op is experimental (invite codes; internet play needs a configured service).
Defaults are borderless at the monitor's desktop resolution with a 30 FPS cap. F1 releases or recaptures the mouse; F6 reloads graphics.ini; F7 cycles the performance overlay.

game_files.label: Ultima Underworld 1 data files
game_files.description: The original game data from a copy you own. Either the DOS assets or the WinCE (Pocket PC) assets work. Extract them into a folder named UWDATA with subfolders DATA, DATA3D, SOUND, CRIT and CUTS, then point the game at it with --data-dir.
game_files.notes: Layout from the README: DATA/ (*.GR *.DAT *.BYT *.SYS *.PAK *.ARK *.CFG *.TR *.CM), DATA3D/ (*.E), SOUND/ (SOUNDS.DAT *.MOD VOC*.wav), CRIT/ (CR*PAGE.N00/N01 ASSOC.ANM), CUTS/ (CS*.N0x). UU.exe and gx.dll are unused leftovers of extraction. Run the game with: ./uw --data-dir [data-path]

first_run: Extract the release zip.
Put your original game data in a UWDATA-style folder with the DATA, DATA3D, SOUND, CRIT and CUTS subfolders.
Run the game with --data-dir pointing at that folder (./uw --data-dir [data-path]).
notes: The port is based on a decompile of the Pocket PC (WinCE) version of Ultima Underworld 1.
Press F for mouselook, G for a fullscreen mode that hides most of the HUD, and ~ to open the debug panel and console (type help for commands).
Releases are labeled a Test Release.
unsure: The README doesn't name the executable inside the release zip; the build instructions refer to ./uw.
No file checksums, region or version requirements are stated for the game data.
The README doesn't say how the release zip is laid out or whether it needs extra libraries such as SDL2.

game_files.label: Monster Hunter 4 Ultimate game dump (USA)
game_files.description: Your own decrypted dump of the USA version of Monster Hunter 4 Ultimate (Nintendo 3DS), made from your cartridge or eShop purchase with GodMode9. The launcher's Setup screen asks for it and remembers it.
game_files.notes: Title ID 0004000000126300. Only the USA version is supported; the European and Japanese versions are not (yet). The dump must be decrypted.

game_files.label: Monster Hunter 4 Ultimate v1.3.0 update (USA)
game_files.description: The v1.3.0 update of the USA game as a .cia, dumped from your own console (GodMode9 can build one from the installed title). The port's recompiled code is built from this update.
game_files.notes: The launcher installs it into Azahar for you and uses it to build the game's code library. The update's own folder id is 0004000E00126300.

first_run: Extract mh4u-port-linux.tar.gz.
Install Python 3.10 or newer, and clang if you have it (otherwise the build can download Zig's compiler, about 80 MB, with --fetch-compiler).
Run mh4u.AppImage. On first run the launcher opens on Setup: choose your decrypted game, install the v1.3.0 update from your .cia, and build the code library.
Alternative: run build-code-library.sh from the package, then install the update yourself.
Press Play.
notes: Not a normal download-and-play port: first run builds the game's code library from your update .cia (a couple of minutes to recompile, several more to compile). It happens once, and again after adding, changing or removing a code mod.
Needs Python 3.10 or newer, used by the setup to build the game's code.
Save states do not work (save in the game). Cheats that rewrite code do not apply; cheats that change data do.
Runs on Azahar's 3DS core; it shares Azahar's user folder (saves, update, mh4u.ini).
Only USA v1.3.0 (title 0004000000126300) is supported.
unsure: The README does not state hashes or exact sizes for the game dump or the update.
The exact layout inside the release archives is not listed; the docs only name mh4u.exe (Windows), mh4u.AppImage (Linux) and MH4U.app (macOS).
The Linux and macOS builds are described as not tried much (macOS not tried on a Mac yet, Steam Deck not tried).

mods.notes: The launcher's Mods screen manages a mod library (on/off, order, conflicts, add a folder or a .zip) and has a catalog of recommended mods and texture packs (MH4U HD texture pack by mhondeck, MH4HDUI, 100% crafting success, Guard Point mods). The library is mh4u-mods/ in Azahar's user folder; mods are deployed to load/mods/0004000000126300/. Texture packs need custom textures turned on. Only one code mod can be active at a time, and code mods need the code library rebuilt. anco's data patch: https://codeberg.org/anco/mh4u_qol

game_files.label: LovePlus+ cartridge dump (Japanese, BOXJ)
game_files.description: A dump of your own LovePlus+ Nintendo DS cartridge, Japanese release, game code BOXJ, as an .nds file. On first run the app asks for it and reads the game's data into its own folder. The .nds file is never modified.
game_files.notes: lp-engine contains nothing from the game; the English translation ships as a delta that applies only to your copy. Only the Japanese BOXJ release is supported.

first_run: chmod +x the AppImage and run it (a loveplus_0.1.0_amd64.deb is also available: sudo apt install ./loveplus_0.1.0_amd64.deb).
When asked, choose your LovePlus+ (BOXJ) .nds file and wait a few seconds while it is read.
notes: The first start asks for your .nds file, then takes a few seconds to read it; after that the game starts straight away.
Complete English translation (a few spots keep their Japanese on purpose), up to 4x resolution, anti-aliasing and upscaled textures.
Wireless features (Talk Mode, card exchange, pass-by communication, save send/receive, regional capsules) are not supported and need a second DS.
Saves are ordinary files: you can import a cartridge or DeSmuME save (.sav / .dsv) and export it back.
The in-game clock follows your computer's clock; a Clock setting shifts it.
unsure: The README does not give hashes or the size of the expected .nds dump.
The macOS zip is described as Apple silicon or Intel; the README does not say whether it is a universal build.
The settings file name is not stated (settings live in the per-user folder).
